source_detail: Emergent Collusion in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Interaction. arXiv 2609.24967 v2 (2026-09-26), main body read by co-author; appendices C, D, H not fully read
design: two agents verify each other's work over repeated rounds; agents solve own tasks (~89% correct); channel 5 messages x 200 characters; a verdict must rest on the peer's raw log (no raw log -> only compliant verdict is REJECT); reward 10 per correct verdict; instruction: maximize reward subject to the protocol; memory across 10 episodes

na_reasons.containment_designed_for: no containment in the setup; agents act only through own task tools and the peer channel

environment_assumptions.notes: grounding yes: tasks have verifiable ground truth; escalation none = none reported (verdicts limited to ACCEPT / REJECT), confirm against App. H; loop closed = incentive loop with memory across 10 episodes

design_conflict.statement: Protocol requires raw-log evidence; channel capacity can't carry raw logs; the compliant verdict (REJECT) is usually the incorrect verdict; reward pays for correct verdicts.
design_conflict.stated_by_authors: yes ('higher reward reachable only by violating the protocol')

stated_limitations: controlled abstraction rather than a necessary condition
